topic_summary: Analysis of the euthanasia and physician-assisted suicide debate, examining the structural collision between autonomy-primary and sanctity-of-life-primary readings of end-of-life decision-making authority. The debate centers on incompatible victim sets: the suffering-prolonged (patients denied choice to end unbearable suffering) versus the pressured-vulnerable (elderly, disabled, and economically disadvantaged populations at risk of coercion or devaluation).

key_entities: Terminally ill patients (primary stakeholders requesting assisted dying)
Healthcare professionals (physicians, palliative care providers with divided opinions)
Disability Rights Education and Defense Fund (advocacy organization opposing legalization)
American Medical Association (institutional opposition, physician role as healer)
Legal jurisdictions (Netherlands, Belgium, Canada, Switzerland, 9 U.S. states + D.C.)
Palliative care institutions (Canadian Society of Palliative Care Physicians)
key_tensions: Individual autonomy vs societal protection of vulnerable populations
Physician role as healer vs physician as facilitator of chosen death
Right to die vs duty to die (resource pressure concern)
key_mechanisms: Progressive eligibility expansion (Netherlands, Belgium, Canada empirical pattern)
Slippery slope pathway (competent terminal → incompetent non-terminal)
Coercion gradient (economic/familial pressure on vulnerable populations)
Palliative care gatekeeping (assessment separation from MAiD eligibility)
key_absences: Empirical data on actual coercion rates in jurisdictions with legal assisted dying
Comparative suffering metrics between jurisdictions with/without legal access

omegas.description: Are actual coercion rates in legal jurisdictions measurably higher than baseline? Research context lacks comparative data. Sanctity_reading's victim set (pressured-vulnerable) may be theoretical rather than empirical.
Is prolonged suffering in prohibition jurisdictions quantifiable? Autonomy_reading's victim set (suffering-prolonged) lacks comparative suffering metrics across legal regimes.

Is progressive expansion (Netherlands/Belgium/Canada pattern) a necessary consequence of autonomy frameworks, or jurisdiction-specific? Slippery_slope_mechanism may be a contingent snare rather than structural necessity.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium: model operates within legalization-as-binary frame; gradual expansion may be policy choice rather than structural inevitability)

omegas.description: Does physician participation in assisted dying erode healer identity (AMA claim) or expand it to include suffering relief? Tension between institutional position and individual physician willingness suggests role definition is contested, not fixed.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence: physician identity as variable rather than constant)

omegas.description: Does the Nazi euthanasia program historical shadow constitute valid structural evidence, or is it a category error (state-imposed murder vs individual choice)? Sanctity arguments invoke this precedent; autonomy arguments reject analogy.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan: who benefits from Nazi analogy? Sanctity advocates gain rhetorical leverage; autonomy advocates lose legitimacy)

commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between individual autonomy (patient as sole legitimate authority) and sanctity-of-life principle (life preservation as categorical constraint on individual choice)

readings.commitment: Individual autonomy grounds the right to control circumstances and timing of death when facing unbearable suffering
readings.expected_structural_delta: Suffering-prolonged enter victim set (patients denied choice); high suppression of paternalistic restrictions; eligibility criteria expand over time (empirical pattern)

readings.expected_structural_delta: Pressured-vulnerable enter victim set (elderly, disabled, economically disadvantaged at coercion risk); categorical prohibition on assisted dying; physician role limited to life preservation

readings.expected_structural_delta: Incompetent patients enter victim set; eligibility criteria drift from terminal-only to chronic suffering; autonomy framework becomes vehicle for sanctity concerns

axiom_contradictions.basis: Autonomy reading holds that individual choice is the sole legitimate authority over one's death; sanctity reading holds that life preservation is a categorical constraint that overrides individual choice. No single coherent framework can simultaneously hold both that individual autonomy is supreme in end-of-life decisions AND that life preservation categorically prohibits those decisions.
